question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "increased diuresis" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "decreased peritubular reabsorption of water" -> "increased diuresis" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "contraction of efferent arteriole" -> "increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "increased diuresis" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "increased renal blood flow" -> "increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "increased diuresis" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "contraction of afferent arteriole" -> "possible decrease in glomerular filtration rate" -> "unclear effect on diuresis" -> 50%
analysis: An increase in blood pressure typically leads to an increase in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) due to increased renal perfusion pressure. This results in increased diuresis. However, the most direct mechanism by which increased blood pressure leads to increased diuresis is through decreased peritubular reabsorption of water. When blood pressure is elevated, the hydrostatic pressure in the peritubular capillaries increases, reducing the reabsorption of water and solutes back into the bloodstream, thereby increasing urine output.
